explanation.title: Spanish Present Tense: Regular & Irregular Verbs

sections.subtitle: Verb Groups & Infinitives
sections.content:
📚 Three Conjugation Groups

1️⃣ -AR verbs:
• hablar (to speak)
• cantar (to sing)
• bailar (to dance)

2️⃣ -ER verbs:
• comer (to eat)
• beber (to drink)
• leer (to read)

3️⃣ -IR verbs:
• vivir (to live)
• escribir (to write)
• abrir (to open)

💡 Infinitive = base form
= 'to (verb)'

✅ Each group has its own endings

sections.subtitle: Regular Present Tense Conjugation
sections.content:
🔧 Remove ending + add new ending

-AR endings (hablar):
• yo → -o (hablo)
• tú → -as (hablas)
• él/ella/usted → -a (habla)
• nosotros → -amos (hablamos)
• vosotros → -áis (habláis)
• ellos/ustedes → -an (hablan)

-ER endings (comer):
• yo → -o (como)
• tú → -es (comes)
• él/ella/usted → -e (come)
• nosotros → -emos (comemos)
• vosotros → -éis (coméis)
• ellos/ustedes → -en (comen)

-IR endings (vivir):
• yo → -o (vivo)
• tú → -es (vives)
• él/ella/usted → -e (vive)
• nosotros → -imos (vivimos)
• vosotros → -ís (vivís)
• ellos/ustedes → -en (viven)

sections.subtitle: Common Irregular Verbs
sections.content:
⚠️ Key Irregular Verbs

SER (to be - permanent):
• soy, eres, es, somos, sois, son

ESTAR (to be - temporary):
• estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están

IR (to go):
• voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van

TENER (to have):
• tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tenéis, tienen

HACER (to do/make):
• hago, haces, hace, hacemos, hacéis, hacen

💡 These are completely irregular
→ Must memorize each form!

sections.subtitle: Stem-Changing Verbs
sections.content:
🔄 Vowel Changes in Stem

⚠️ All forms EXCEPT nosotros/vosotros

1️⃣ E → IE:
• pensar (to think)
  → pienso, piensas, piensa
  → pensamos (✅ no change)
  → piensan

2️⃣ O → UE:
• poder (to be able)
  → puedo, puedes, puede
  → podemos (✅ no change)
  → pueden

3️⃣ E → I (mainly -IR verbs):
• pedir (to ask for)
  → pido, pides, pide
  → pedimos (✅ no change)
  → piden

💡 Change happens in stressed syllable

sections.subtitle: First Person Irregulars
sections.content:
🔥 Irregular in YO form only

-GO verbs:
• tener → tengo
• poner → pongo
• salir → salgo
• venir → vengo
• hacer → hago
• decir → digo

-ZCO verbs:
• conocer → conozco
• traducir → traduzco
• ofrecer → ofrezco

Other:
• saber → sé
• ver → veo
• dar → doy

✅ All other forms are regular!

sections.subtitle: Present Progressive
sections.content:
🏃 Actions Happening RIGHT NOW

Formula: ESTAR + gerund

Form gerund:
• -AR verbs → -ando
  → hablar → hablando
• -ER/-IR verbs → -iendo
  → comer → comiendo
  → vivir → viviendo

Examples:
• Estoy comiendo → I am eating
• Están hablando → They are talking
• Estamos estudiando → We are studying

⚠️ Use for actions IN PROGRESS
❌ NOT for habitual actions
• Como pan → I eat bread (habitual)
• Estoy comiendo pan → I'm eating bread (now)

questions.question: What are the three Spanish verb groups?
questions.hint: Each group is based on the infinitive ending. Think: hablar, comer, vivir.

questions.question: What is the 'yo' form of 'hablar' (to speak)?
questions.hint: Remove -ar and add -o for yo form of -AR verbs.

questions.question: What is the 'nosotros' form of 'comer' (to eat)?
questions.hint: Remove -er and add -emos for nosotros form of -ER verbs.

questions.question: What is the 'tú' form of 'vivir' (to live)?
questions.hint: Remove -ir and add -es for tú form of -IR verbs.

questions.question: What is the 'yo' form of SER (to be)?
questions.hint: This is completely irregular. It's one of the most common verbs in Spanish.

questions.question: What is the 'yo' form of ESTAR (to be)?
questions.hint: This is the other 'to be' verb. The yo form is completely irregular.

questions.question: What is the 'yo' form of IR (to go)?
questions.hint: This is completely irregular and doesn't look like the infinitive at all.

questions.question: What is the 'yo' form of TENER (to have)?
questions.hint: This is a -GO verb irregular in the yo form. It also has a stem change in other forms.

questions.question: What is the 'yo' form of HACER (to do/make)?
questions.hint: This is a -GO verb. The yo form ends in -go.

questions.question: What happens to 'pensar' (e→ie) in the 'yo' form?
questions.hint: The 'e' in the stem changes to 'ie' when stressed. Add -o for yo form.

questions.question: What happens to 'poder' (o→ue) in the 'tú' form?
questions.hint: The 'o' in the stem changes to 'ue' when stressed. Add -es for tú form.

questions.question: Does 'pensar' have a stem change in the 'nosotros' form?
questions.hint: Nosotros and vosotros forms do NOT have stem changes. The stress is not on the stem.

questions.question: What is the 'yo' form of 'pedir' (e→i)?
questions.hint: E→I stem changes are mainly in -IR verbs. The 'e' changes to 'i' when stressed.

questions.question: What is the 'yo' form of 'poner' (to put)?
questions.hint: This is a -GO verb, irregular only in the yo form.

questions.question: What is the 'yo' form of 'salir' (to leave/go out)?
questions.hint: Another -GO verb. The yo form ends in -go.

questions.question: What is the 'yo' form of 'conocer' (to know)?
questions.hint: This is a -ZCO verb. The yo form adds 'zc' before the -o ending.

questions.question: What is the 'yo' form of 'saber' (to know)?
questions.hint: This is completely irregular in the yo form. It's very short!

questions.question: How do you form the gerund of -AR verbs?
questions.hint: Hablar → hablando. The gerund for -AR verbs ends in -ando.

questions.question: How do you form the gerund of -ER and -IR verbs?
questions.hint: Comer → comiendo, vivir → viviendo. Both -ER and -IR use -iendo.

questions.question: How do you say 'I am eating' (right now)?
questions.hint: Use estar + gerund for the present progressive. Conjugate estar, then add the gerund of comer.

questions.question: What does 'Están hablando' mean?
questions.hint: Estar + gerund indicates an action in progress right now.

questions.question: When do you use present progressive vs simple present?

answers.text: Progressive for actions happening now, simple for habits
Progressive for habits, simple for now

questions.hint: Use 'estoy comiendo' for eating RIGHT NOW. Use 'como' for 'I eat' (in general/habitually).
